name: Fondation CAB
funding: Founder Hubert Bonnet (Forges de Clabecq steel heir, real estate) funds it. Partners: Pictet, BNP Paribas Fortis, De Bethune, Duvel. Members pay EUR 500 to 2,000.

name: La Loge
funding: Flemish Government, French Community, VGC, Ixelles, COCOF, Brussels-Capital Region and the National Lottery, plus First Sight members.

name: Wiels Contemporary Art Centre
funding: Flemish, French-speaking, Brussels and VGC governments. Structural partners: Duvel Moortgat, Phillips, Aureus Ars & Scientia. Exhibition partners include Loterie Nationale and Gulbenkian France; GBL supports education.

name: iMAL
funding: Small art-and-tech centre (2025) with structural funding from Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, Flanders and VGC, plus the National Lottery and the ERDF.

name: Museum Dhondt-Dhaenens
funding: Flemish Government, Sint-Martens-Latem and the National Lottery. Partners include Christie's, Duvel, Puilaetco, Zwartopwit, Colora Gent, Jet Import and the Willame foundation.

name: KIOSK
funding: Project support from Schleich-Lentz Foundation and Konschthal Esch.

name: S.M.A.K.
funding: City of Ghent and Flanders. Current partners include the National Lottery, Belfius, Jan De Nul, Interparking, Christie's, Hiscox and Duvel. ENGIE has supported art workshops since 2012.

name: Z33
funding: Kunstenhuis of the Province of Limburg.

name: Contour Biennale
funding: Flemish Community and City of Mechelen, with Kunsthal Mechelen as main partner. 2026 international partners include the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, Mondriaan Fund, Acción Cultural Española and several embassies.
